acceptance_gates: Required player journeys work end to end in the real client.
Character, inventory, currency, quest and social state persist correctly across logout and restart.
Material defects have regression tests; relevant protocol, server and database checks pass.
Content and balance rules have compatible publisher or pinned-client evidence.
Required features and reference-data gaps are resolved; deployed builds are verified separately from source builds.

work_order.journey: Login, create a neutral level-one character, enter the world, move, use an NPC, accept a quest, fight, receive loot and EXP, equip an item, die, revive, return to character selection and relog.
work_order.remaining_verification: Repeat the whole journey with the deployed client and SQL-backed servers, then verify the saved state after restart.
Verify the supported class skill trees, weapons and consumables, effects, monster AI and HP/MP behaviour against the selected client and compatible reference rules.

Resolve missing quest graphs, NPCs, monster populations, portal links, drop rules and uncertified non-EXP progression fields. Refresh inventories before using their historical counts as current measurements.
Verify shops, repairs, crafting, warehouse, trade, personal stores, mail and auctions with durable item/currency ownership and interruption/restart cases.
Verify parties and loot modes, guilds, companions, travel between channels and maps, PvP and the required official event modes in multi-client sessions.

known_implementation_gaps.detail: Hosted logical channels now switch through the full World teleport cycle on one map server, preserving character state and exchanging channel-specific visibility. Map regressions and World socket routing tests cover both directions, blocked destinations, pending transfers, summons and cast replay. Source is deployed with logical channel 1 hosted; real multi-channel/pinned-client verification remains pending; shared physical/global maps and multi-map-server handoff need separate topology work.

Weapon-slot, kind-mask and durability-power checks now precede atomic ammo/required-item consumption on ordinary casts, loops and act-item skills. Per-inventory ammo aggregation and the base-plus-additional-hit rule follow the inherited implementation. 36 gameplay regressions pass; a live read-only SQL check confirms ammo kind/count on 142 templates. Legacy infinite-ammo IDs absent from the pinned item catalogue are not exemptions. Source is deployed and the deployed library passes the read-only SQL field check. Pinned-client parity and actual logout/restart persistence remain to verify. Ordinary cast wear and active-effect prerequisites are implemented in the following entries.

Caster previous-active effects gate actions, ordinary casts and act items; loops use the caster target-active field. Targets require their effect at impact, for damage, buffs and cures. Learned-only or expired effects do not satisfy the requirement. The pinned client's fields agree on the 765 shared SQL IDs except skill 201's target effect, restored from 0 to 200 by migration 040. That migration passes five temporary-table scenarios and is now applied to live SQL; a read-only probe using the deployed library verifies all fields on 765 skills and 27 options. Gameplay in the pinned client is pending.

Accepted ordinary casts wear chart-selected gear; incoming landed damage wears a shield on block or one armor slot on positive HP loss, before HP/MP loss and including lethal hits. Break/deletion messages, stat refresh and persistence are shared. Natural wear preserves indestructible gear. Hostile-side item reactions can modify damage, reflect it or authorize the rolled level-one counter-skill against the attacker. Player impact replay cannot repeat wear/reactions. 32 defensive-equipment cases now supplement the earlier 46 prerequisite/cast-wear cases; the map solution passes 1438 tests on Linux. Live SQL currently has no configured automatic option-skill links. Source is deployed. Expected official assignments, inherited probabilities, pinned-client gameplay and real logout/restart persistence remain to verify.

known_implementation_gaps.area: World return of lifedrain and reflected damage
known_implementation_gaps.detail: The missing MW_GETBLOOD_REQ receiver now completes the existing Map-to-World route. HP/MP gains cap without overflow, dead objects cannot revive, and reflection leaves at least 1 HP without recursive reactions. The main route/key and target object ownership/map/channel are checked for players, hosted monsters and own recall/self/companion objects. 39 return-path regressions pass, including stale routes, foreign objects and rejection on the client port. Source is deployed; real multi-client gameplay remains pending.

Natural HP recovery now scales personal/party and guild damage credit by the healed share of the previous deficit, erases zero buckets and releases the keeper at the inherited integer 90% threshold. A new attacker can claim EXP and loot. MP-only, blocked, dead and premature HP passes do not change credit; aggro, host, loot locks and scheduled AI identity remain. Monster appearance and claim/release, mode and fort-capture notifications use each viewer's faction and party/private keeper colour. History was inspected before editing; transition-only recovery anchors, O(1) cancellation and the next-war fort fix remain. All 35 new cases and 1492 map-solution tests pass. Source is deployed and migration 040 is applied in the same release. Pinned-client playthrough and independent publisher-rule parity remain pending.

reference_limitations: The pinned original client's exact release is unknown.
Complete official server-side spawn, probability and balance data has not been established.
Inherited private-server data and implemented C++ behaviour require independent parity evidence.
